abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are promising non-invasive biomarkers, but their clinical application is limited by inefficient isolation and downstream analysis. Here, we developed a biomimetic magnetic cilia microfluidic chip (MagCilia-chip) for EV capture and proteomic profiling from urine. Tim4-functionalized magnetic microcilia specifically captured phosphatidylserine-positive EVs and underwent magnetic-field-driven three-dimensional rotation to enhance EV-microstructure interactions. Compared with ultracentrifugation, the MagCilia-chip operated in 3D rotation mode achieved a recovery rate of 85% versus 27%, with 5.32-fold higher EV yield and 3.13-fold higher purity. On-chip lysis and digestion followed by mass-spectrometry analysis identified 2903 EV-derived proteins from 50 μL of urine. In the discovery cohort of 12 prostate cancer (PCa) and 8 post-treatment (PT) samples, 368 differentially expressed EV proteins were identified, yielding a five-protein candidate panel. Independent parallel reaction monitoring analysis of 19 PCa and 9 PT samples confirmed differential expression of C9, COL6A3, and VTN. A three-protein panel achieved area-under-the-curve values of 0.78-0.95 across ten machine-learning classifiers using leave-one-out cross-validation. This platform provides an efficient strategy for urinary EV isolation and proteomic analysis and supports further evaluation of EV-derived candidate biomarkers for PCa treatment.
